summary: EXP-B check B6 compared entropy-rate estimates across representations with tolerance 0.01 bit. It passed, but the state-Markov source differed by 0.0089 bit because plug-in estimates in the transition representation converge slowly (hidden-Markov structure). The check could not have distinguished a real difference from estimator lag.
resolution: Replace with exact entropy rates from generating models or convergence-aware estimators (OP-008, Q-001).

summary: The 'spread' metric (max circular distance of differing bits from the injection site) conflates displacement with growth: rule 170 (pure shift, damage size constant 1) reaches max spread 8, the same as the chaotic rule 30. Rejected as a measure of propagation extent; the values remain in EXP-D artifacts, reinterpreted as 'reach'.
resolution: Q-002: damage-support width and light-cone speed.

summary: EXP-G's toy program outputs a checksum that depends on every data bit, so logical masking in unprotected storage was 0%. Reported naively, this would have suggested 'unprotected single flips are never logically masked'. It is a property of the chosen output observable. Caught at the first execution; the post-hoc G8 analysis per observable was added (H-014).

Leading-order asymptotic E[#components] ~ (1/2) ln n predicts 4.16 at n=4096; measured mean 4.665 (+12%). The leading-order formula is not adequate at this n (a constant-order correction matters). It was deliberately not used as a pass/fail check; cyclic-node and tail checks passed (-6.3%, -0.15%).

H-001 (history carries predictive information beyond the current state, universally) is disproven by the iid and state-Markov sources. It survives only as the definition of non-Markovianity in a representation.
H-002, information-content form (transitions carry information not present in states), is disproven. The recoding loses exactly 1 bit.
H-010's dominance prediction ('on-cycle effect >> off-cycle effect') had no numeric falsification threshold, so it cannot be promoted beyond SIMULATED despite a large observed gap.
resolution: Pre-register a threshold (e.g. ratio > 10 on fresh seeds) in a follow-up run.

summary: Found during bootstrap, before any recorded run: (a) experiment modules imported substrate.trace.run and then defined run(config), which shadowed it and would have caused self-recursion; (b) a str.format template contained literal braces. Both fixed; tests/test_reproducibility.py now executes every experiment twice.

The epistemic guard matched the forbidden word 'proven' as a substring, so any claim mentioning 'provenance' was rejected (H-015, DISC-006 at R2). This is a false positive, which fails safe but blocks legitimate claims. Fixed with a whole-word regex and a regression test. Validation of the validation system found a defect the designed test cases had missed.

The value-address envelope's deterministic_sha256 hashed (address, kind, value) together, so it identified the address-bound result, not the value; Store.compare used it for different addresses, so the verdict 'same_value' was unreachable: /map/increment/3/power/8/table vs /map/eca/204/3/table (one table) and /space/8/state/5 vs /map/eca/90/8/state/5 were reported 'different_value'. Reproduced before the fix. Resolved by decomposing identity into address_id, derivation_id (computable from the typed term without evaluation), value_id (canonical value per kind; None when not materialized), environment_id and an execution hash; compare now uses value_id across addresses. deterministic_sha256 is kept with its actual semantics stated. Regression tests: tests/test_purl_terms.py, including an independent hash oracle.
